name: Renato Carneiro
event: UFC Fight Night: Moicano vs. Nolan
summary: Renato 'Moicano' Carneiro (21-7-1, age 37) is a veteran Brazilian lightweight and former title challenger: a high-level opportunistic jiu-jitsu player with better boxing than his record suggests. He's back in the win column after submitting Chris Duncan in round two in April, and takes Tom Nolan on about six weeks' notice after Brian Ortega pulled out of their UFC 331 rematch. Every one of his losses at lightweight has come against an elite wrestler or a big puncher.

how_they_fight.Striking: Long, accurate jab (50% significant accuracy) with a straight right behind it. Against Duncan he worked the jab and clinch in round one and dropped him with a left hook in round two (per Sherdog; our verified fight data doesn't record that knockdown). He also dropped Beneil Dariush with a straight right late in round one at UFC 317 (Cageside Press). Sherdog's Ben Duffy rates him a better striker than his record suggests. His two TKO wins (Jalin Turner, Benoit Saint-Denis) both came in 2024, both in round two.
how_they_fight.Grappling: This is his real weapon. Eleven of his 21 wins are submissions. He hunts the back quickly when an opponent is hurt or scrambling (Duncan, face crank or RNC depending on the outlet, 3:14 of R2; Sherdog says face crank, LowKick says rear-naked choke). Duffy calls his ground-and-pound 'underratedly nasty' and says he does his best work on top; he wrestles better offensively than his frame suggests (about 1.6 takedowns per 15 minutes).
how_they_fight.Defense: Takedown defense is the hole (about 55%). Makhachev, Dariush and Rafael dos Anjos all beat him by putting him on his back: Dariush went 5-for-5 on takedowns with almost six minutes of control, and dos Anjos held him down for over 13 minutes across five rounds. He was knocked out three times at 145/155 (Chan Sung Jung R1, Rafael Fiziev R1, Jose Aldo R2), all against high-level strikers, the last in 2020.
how_they_fight.Pace & cardio: A front-to-middle-round finisher. His 13 stoppage wins came 4 in R1, 8 in R2 and only 1 in R3 (2010); his last seven finishes all came in R1 or R2. His five stoppage losses: three in R1 (Jung KO, Fiziev TKO, Makhachev sub), one in R2 (Aldo TKO), one in R3 (Brian Ortega guillotine, 2017, a fight he was winning). His only five-round fight was the 2022 decision loss to dos Anjos, where he was controlled for most of it. Against Dariush he won R1, then got taken down and lost R2-R3. At 37, how he holds up in rounds 4-5 is an open question.
how_they_fight.Fight IQ: Experienced and opportunistic, and quick to pounce on a hurt opponent. Brash outside the cage. Took this fight calling Nolan the harder opponent than Ortega and saying 'it is what it is' (Uncrowned).

patterns: Jab-led boxing to set up takedowns and scrambles
Jumps on the back the moment an opponent is hurt; 11 career submissions
Finishes come early: 12 of 13 stoppage wins in R1-R2, the last seven all inside two rounds
Loses when out-wrestled and held down (dos Anjos, Makhachev, Dariush) or caught by elite punchers (Jung, Fiziev, Aldo)
Strong first round, fades when he spends time on his back (Dariush won R2-R3)
concerns: Age 37, with a long career's worth of wear (Sherdog)
Takedown defense against a big, strong opponent
One career five-round fight, and he lost it on the mat
Short-notice change of opponent: he'd prepared for Ortega, a different body type and style from the 6-foot-3 Nolan
keys_to_beat: Wrestle him and hold top position; make him carry weight into the later rounds
Respect his scrambles: don't give up the back when getting up
Survive his first two rounds, then push the pace in the championship rounds

news.text: Brian Ortega withdrew from their UFC 331 rematch with a cut over his left eye, the second time he'd pulled out of the fight this year. Moicano was moved to headline this card against Tom Nolan.
Moicano said Nolan will be a harder fight than Ortega would have been, and that he won't book Ortega again (Uncrowned).
MMA Weekly headline: Moicano volunteered to be Ilia Topuria's tune-up fight when Topuria returns.
Submitted Chris Duncan at 3:14 of R2 (Sherdog: face crank) to end a two-fight losing streak.
